newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Bourses sag but dollar weathers trade shock.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bourses sag but dollar weathers trade shock.

text.p: Europe's major equity markets and Wall Street all sagged on Wednesday but the dollar appeared to weather a big surge in Japan's trade surplus relatively well.
Both the London and Paris bourses were down more than one percent at one point during the morning but they pulled off their lows during the afternoon despite the Dow opening weak.

The dollar briefly fell through 113 yen in European afternoon trade, revisiting levels seen in Asia, but it recovered later and traders said it was fairly resilient in the face of a report showing Japan's trade surplus surged again in May.
Japan's Finance Ministry said the surplus zoomed more than 220 percent in May from a year earlier and the balance with the United States rose 93 percent.
"Dollar/yen seems to be sidelined as the downside seems to be somewhat protected," said Bob Near, a vice president on the corporate trading desk at the Bank of New York.
European traders said they were wary of adding to their short dollar positions before a meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) leading industrial nations that starts on Friday.
By 1415 GMT the dollar was quoted at 1.7255 marks and 113.04 yen, compared with 1.7335 and 113.37 in late European trade on Tuesday.

Equity markets saw London's blue-chip FTSE 100 index continue this week's steep falls, unable to shake off worries over the new Labour government's first budget next month and pushed lower by stronger-than-expected consumer spending figures.
Fears that the government will scrap an important tax break for pension funds has triggered a big selloff this week.
"People are using every excuse to do nothing today and the futures have been a big technical downer," one trader said.
"We've got the budget and more worries about interest rates, so we'll probably see people sitting on their hands until July."
The Office for National Statistics said retail sales grew by 1.8 percent in the three months to May compared with the previous three months, the highest quarterly rate of growth since July 1988.
Economists said the figures showed that large windfall gains made by millions of people following the conversion of mutual home loan societies into banks were working their way into the marketplace.

"Unless we get a very tight budget, I think an interest rate hike is likely at the next meeting (of the Treasury and Bank of England). This is bad news for gilts and clearly suggests the economy's still growing above trend," Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International, said.
Paris fared no better than London, with traders citing investor caution ahead of new Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's parliamentary debut on Thursday.
"Jospin's speaking tomorrow. We're waiting for the flavour of what he says," said one trader as the CAC-40 index fell 24.71 points, or 0.89 percent, at 2,737.89 by 1415 GMT.

Drink and luxury goods group LVMH came off its lows but remained 2.54 percent down at 1,494 francs after announcing on Tuesday it had bought 0.23 percent of GrandMet GMET.PA but was not planning to make an offer for the British drinks company.
Germany's 30-share DAX index also weakened, but less than its major European rivals, closing down 11.21 points, or 0.3 percent, at 3,730.27 during bourse floor trade.
The IBIS DAX lost further ground in later screen trading after the Dow Jones industrial average opened lower.
Traders said the market was unable to cobble together any upward impetus in the absence of inspirational new corporate data.
CURRENCIES AT 1415 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7255 marks and 113.04 yen, compared with 1.7335 and 113.37 in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1415 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 29.8 points, or 0.64 percent, at 4,652.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 21.83 points, or 0.79 percent, at 2,740.77.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 11.21 points, or 0.3 percent, at 3,730.27.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $341.60 against $342.05 in the morning. Platinum was $10 eaisier at $409.50, while palladium was down $6.50 at $191.50.
